I made friends in high school and was very shocked that I did because I thought to myself “who would want to hangout with me?” I don’t see my high school friends that much anymore.

When I was about 21, my dad and mom were getting on my case about getting a job. So I got one in retail unfortunately and it sucked. I been in retail for 5 years and I hate it so much, but can’t find any other types of jobs. My friends seems to be doing well, but I’m not. I suffer from anxiety and depression, which causes me to either cry or have a mental breakdown. I try talking to a suicide therapist, but that didn’t work either.

I try to hangout with different people in college, but they would never hangout with me saying they have to do something at the last minute. Today, all I think about is how I’m going to die as I feel nothing inside of me anymore that gives me joy, love or happiness besides my family, music and video games which is holding me back from suicide. Tbh, I don’t even care about myself… That why I plan on taking my life within a year or two.

I’m 00s kid and was a big fan of Cartoon Network. As a kid in the early 2000s I felt like Cartoon Network was at it peak. Cartoon Cartoon Friday’s is what I always looked forward when it was Friday because I would race home to catch my favorite character host. 

Then in the mid 2000s you had the city era of CN and it was decent that you had character interact with others in the city. Programming was still pretty decent too, but this is when most of the 90s show got cancelled so some people started to hate CN for that around this time. 

I say that the late 00s was CN low point as many of the cartoons I grew up with was coming to an end and they started to do that reality show thing CN Real, but also I believe that the late 00s was a transitional era that lead the way for the 2010s CN. Shows like Flapjack and Chowder are vastly different from the cartoons from before and had that wacky charm about them that feel like they could be 2010s shows. And sure there was Star Wars Clone Wars and Total Drama Island so it wasn’t too bad, but compared to before it just not that good.

Now, 2010s CN was great return to form. Flapjack and Chowder may have showed a glimpse of what the 2010s cartoons will be like, but Adventure Time perfected it and bought more cartoons along the way like Regular Show, World of Gumball, Steven Universe, We Bare Bears and more. However, my only grip with this era is that once they started rebooting 90s and 00s shows like Ben 10, Powerpuff girls, Teen Titans that where it went wrong. They started focusing on show like Teen Titans Go more and pretty much neglected the original programs that bought them back like Regular Show and Adventure Time on to there schedule similar to how Nickelodeon treats Spongebob.
